Mr. Qumrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, places the texts of the impugned notice line-by-line before the Court and submits that the same is full of ambiguity and, thus, an ordinary person, like the petitioner, would not be able to comprehend its contentions. In an endeavor to elaborate his submissions on this point, he pinpoints to the Cause Title of the impugned notice which contains the word 'appeal' as well as the word 'revision' in chorus and submits that if those words are taken in their true sense employing their literal meanings, then the impugned order is liable to be declared illegal on the face of it inasmuch as there is no provision anywhere in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (SAT Act) empowering respondent No.3 to rehear an appeal.
